106-progress.name: Tommy Joe Stonefield
106-progress.text: You have what??  Maybell is the light of my dull life.  Hurry, let me see her letter!
106-progress.title: Young Lovers

107-progress.name: William Pestle
107-progress.text: You have a note from "Gramma" Stonefield, eh?  I haven't seen Mildred in years!  I wonder what she has to say...
107-progress.title: Note to William

109-accept.name: Marshal Dughan
109-accept.text: Looks to me you've seen quite a bit of combat in your time, $c.  If you haven't already, you should report to Gryan Stoutmantle.  He heads up the People's Militia, aimed at protecting the farmlands of $N.  I bet he could use your help.  You can usually find him in the stone tower on Sentinel Hill, just off the road in the middle of $N.
109-accept.title: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle

112-progress.name: William Pestle
112-progress.text: Do you have that crystal kelp?  I'm sure Maybell is anxious to see her beau...
112-progress.title: Collecting Kelp

114-progress.name: Maybell Maclure
114-progress.text: Did you deliver my letter to Tommy Joe?  What did he say??
114-progress.title: The Escape

1688-progress.name: Gakin the Darkbinder
1688-progress.text: Even the older and wiser can be unmanned by the wiles of youth and beauty, $N. A piece of advice you would do well to remember throughout your life.
1688-progress.title: Surena Caledon

1689-progress.name: Gakin the Darkbinder
1689-progress.text: I cannot show you how to control a voidwalker until you have overtaken one.
1689-progress.title: The Binding

184-accept.name: Unknown
184-accept.text:
This is the deed to an expanse of farmlands within $N.  It is signed by a Theodore Furlbrow and cosigned by his wife, Verna.  And on the back of the deed are hastily scrawled words:

"We leaned on Furlbrow and got his deed.  Thought it might be handy if you wanted to forge one of these for your own place.

The Furlbrows won't give us trouble.  Last I saw them they were on their way out of $N, stuck with a broken wagon."

You think the Furlbrows might want their deed back...
184-accept.title: Furlbrow's Deed

76-progress.name: Marshal Dughan
76-progress.text: Hail, $N.  What do you have to report? Have you scouted the Jasperlode Mine?
76-progress.title: The Jasperlode Mine

83-progress.name: Sara Timberlain
83-progress.text: I'm running low on linen, $N.  Do you have any for me?
83-progress.title: Red Linen Goods

84-progress.name: Billy Maclure
84-progress.text: Ugh... I'm starving!  Do you have that pie for me, $N?
84-progress.title: Back to Billy

86-progress.name: "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield
86-progress.text:
I don't think it's right feeding the boy who stole my necklace in the first place, but if that's what it takes to get back what's mine, then so be it!

Do you have that boar meat?
86-progress.title: Pie for Billy

87-progress.name: "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield
87-progress.text: Hello, $N.  Have you found my necklace?
87-progress.title: Goldtooth

88-progress.name: Ma Stonefield
88-progress.text: Did you see her yet?  Did you get her?
88-progress.title: Princess Must Die!

91723-complete.name: Hamish Bergwort
91723-complete.text: Well done, my friend. Let me try my calibrations again...
91723-complete.title: Delicate Instruments

91724-accept.name: Hamish Bergwort
91724-accept.text:
Almost there, and... By the Nether! Something is still disrupting my instruments.
This is most frustrating, $N. I have heard rumors that the local bandits have been practicing spells near Stone Cairn Lake. Maybe if you stop them, these disruptions will finally cease and I can get some work done?
91724-accept.title: Delicate Instruments

91732-complete.name: Hagar Lowe
91732-complete.text: Oh, very nice. Do you see that shine? Truly, they don't make them like they used to.
91732-complete.title: Good Steel

91732-progress.name: Hagar Lowe
91732-progress.text: Have you been to the mine yet?
91732-progress.title: Good Steel

91777-progress.name: Brother Paxton

91777-progress.title: Rare Books

97920-complete.name: Lee Brown
97920-complete.text:
There you have it, you can now craft your very own Fish Bowl. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
